{{Person}}

Alphonse de Lamartine, born in 1790 at Mâcon, was known for his writing and participation in French national politics, first as a moderate supporter of the monarchy, then as a republican calling for fundamental social reforms.<ref>{{#cite:Q1996}}</ref>

== Early life ==

Born into a noble family owner of the vineyard of Milly, Lamartine had an abundant childhood and received systematic education in the Catholic school system.<ref>{{#cite:Q1996}}</ref>

== Political activity ==

In the early years of his career, Lamartine occupied various military and diplomatic offices under Louis XVIII and Charles X thanks to his father's connections and his increasing literary fame, before being elected to the French National Assembly in 1833.<ref>{{#cite:Q1996}}</ref>

=== Abolition of slavery ===

In 1834, Lamartine became one of the 27 cofounders of the French Society for the Abolition of Slavery. In the following years, he made multiple speeches in front of the National Assembly to campaign for the cause.<ref>{{#cite:Q1996}}</ref>

=== Abolition of the death penalty ===

During his 18 years of office at the French national assembly, Lamartine also called repeatedly for the abolition of the death penalty.<ref>{{#cite:Q1996}}</ref>

=== Social reforms ===

On his entry to the French national assembly, preferring complete independence, Lamartine refused to join any political party. "Je siégerai au plafond (I will sit on the ceiling)", he famously joked.<ref>{{#cite:Q1993}}</ref>

Advocating for the National Assembly to focus on "de ce qui peut être utile ou nuisible à la société (things that can be of use or harm to the society)", Lamartine was able to slowly gather supporters around him thanks to his charm and speech, forming a new party of independents, which became known as the "Parti social (social party)".<ref>{{#cite:Q1993}}</ref>

== Writing ==

Today, Lamartine is Often labelled as one of the first "[[romanticism|romantics]]". He wrote numerous poems, reflecting on his life experience, emotions, and christian faith.<ref>{{#cite:Q1993}}</ref>

Some of his most famous poems are collected in his poetic album ''[[Source:Méditations poétiques (Book)|Méditations poétiques]]'', first published in 1820.
